description: Converted to OA-10A; on loan from NMUSAF to NY ANG 174 MXG/MXA; Baugher and Aerial Visuals both record it on display at Syracuse; one of six airframes matching the six OpenStreetMap historic=aircraft nodes clustered at the base entrance on East Molloy Road
museum_name: Hancock Field Air National Guard Base Air Park

description: PAINTED IDENTITY DIFFERS - Baugher records this Block 10 airframe as displayed at Syracuse painted as 80-0205; used for battle-damage-repair training at Syracuse before display; on loan from NMUSAF to 174 MXG/MXA
museum_name: Hancock Field Air National Guard Base Air Park

description: Served 20th FG then Massachusetts ANG 101st FS then 127th PTG and 3750th TTW; previously preserved at Lackland AFB Texas; Baugher gives the Syracuse display period as 1994 to 2002 yet the April 2016 NMUSAF loan list still charges it to NY ANG Syracuse - the conflict is unresolved and its 2025-26 presence is the weakest claim in this block
museum_name: Hancock Field Air National Guard Base Air Park

description: Served 3595th CCTW then Massachusetts ANG 101st TFS then NY ANG 138th TFS from 1967; put on display at the NY ANG base at Syracuse airport; on loan from NMUSAF to 174 MXG/MXA
museum_name: Hancock Field Air National Guard Base Air Park

description: TRUE IDENTITY IS THE PROTOTYPE - built as an F-94B airframe on the production line and completed as the Lockheed Model 880 YF-97A; first flight 19 Jan 1950; later redesignated YF-94C; the April 2016 NMUSAF loan list wrongly calls it an F-94B; on display with NY ANG Syracuse
museum_name: Hancock Field Air National Guard Base Air Park

description: To AMARC as TE0011 16 Sept 1991; returned to service 15 May 2000 with the 174th FW; on display with NY ANG Syracuse; on loan from NMUSAF; Aerial Visuals miscalls it an A-37 - Baugher's T-37B with MSN 40065 is correct
museum_name: Hancock Field Air National Guard Base Air Park
